stem.text: The function h is defined on the closed interval \( [-1, 4] \) and is twice differentiable at every x in that interval except \( x = 0 \), where h has a jump discontinuity. Also \( h'(1) = 0 \) and \( h''(1) > 0 \). Must h attain an absolute minimum value on the closed interval \( [-1, 4] \)? Justify the answer.

answer_key.label: No, because h is not continuous on the closed interval \( [-1, 4] \), so the Extreme Value Theorem does not apply.

worked_solution.text: h has a jump discontinuity at \( x = 0 \), inside the interval, so h is not continuous on \( [-1, 4] \).
A hypothesis of the Extreme Value Theorem fails, so the theorem gives no conclusion and h need not attain an absolute minimum value.
